notes: Eval-as-is harness. Baseline = no skill. Prompts are natural user tasks — they do NOT prescribe change-note format, coverage matrices, or dependency-declaration syntax; producing that discipline unprompted is what discriminates skill from baseline.

evals.name: revision-pass-tension-002-plan-absorption
evals.prompt: Tension 002 got resolved — the canonical TopologyPattern enum is now the spec C-CP-10 §10.1 vocabulary: single-threaded-linear, orchestrator-workers, decentralized-handoff, hierarchical-delegation, evaluator-optimizer, parallelization. U-CP-22 in design-substrate/Implementation_Plan_Control_Plane_v2_1.md needs to absorb that. Update it.
evals.expected_output: Discriminating signal: a revision-pass output — a change-note declaring scope (Tension 002 absorption), sections preserved vs revised, the revised U-CP-22 signature using the spec C-CP-10 §10.1 enum names, acceptance #1/#3 realigned to the spec, spec-traceability cited by ID+section. Must NOT extend the spec (no invented patterns or admissibility semantics) and must surface any residual gap rather than inventing. Baseline likely just edits the enum names without the change-note discipline or the acceptance-#3 admissibility realignment.

evals.name: env-fit-workflow-version-citation
evals.prompt: I need the implementation breakdown for C-IS-02 §2, the artifact-tier layering schema — it's in design-substrate/Spec_Information_Substrate_v1.md. Work out the units.
evals.expected_output: Environment-fit check: the skill body cites 'Workflow v1.5 §7' and 'operates under the V3 system prompt' — neither exists here (canonical is Project_Workflow_v1_8.md; framing is CLAUDE.md). A sound run must not hard-block or cite a phantom v1.5 workflow. The decomposition itself should be sound: atomic units, each spec-traceable to C-IS-02 §2 by ID+section, acyclic dependency declarations. Cross-check: U-IS-03 already implemented this contract — the output should be broadly consistent with the landed harness_is.artifact_tier_registry (5-tier enum + metadata).

evals.name: atomic-decomposition-spec-extension-guard
evals.prompt: Break down C-AS-05 §5 — the fetch_secret contract, in design-substrate/Spec_Action_Surface_v1.md — into implementation units for me.
evals.expected_output: Tests the load-bearing discipline: the planner decomposes, it never extends the spec. If C-AS-05 §5 defers anything to implementation discretion, a passing run surfaces that as a gap rather than inventing the missing commitment (e.g., does not invent a secrets backend, key format, or scope semantics the contract doesn't commit). Units must be atomic, spec-traceable by ID+section, dependency-explicit. Baseline is more likely to invent unspecified implementation detail.
